title: Listen from the Inside Out
coreMove: Set down the internal voice long enough for the other person's meaning to arrive.
sourcePressure: The chapter locates listening inside the listener: notice counterargument, judgment, and identity management before using questions, paraphrase, and acknowledgment.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Equating listening with silence, eye contact, or scripted paraphrase.

sourceAnchors.name: internal voice
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names three internal tasks that block listening: building counterarguments, judging, and managing identity stakes.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The first thing to listen for is often the argument already speaking inside your own head.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.

exampleSpecs.audience: managers whose internal voice is louder than the employee
exampleSpecs.stakes: retention risk is rising because the employee feels unheard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan writes 'counterargument,' 'judgment,' and 'identity' on the margin before asking what has been hardest
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a video-call window with the mute icon lit

exampleSpecs.stakes: a family complaint could reveal a real care gap if judgment quiets down
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida notices her mind saying 'they are being unfair' and sets it aside for one question
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the antiseptic smell of a consultation room

exampleSpecs.domain: partner explaining loneliness after a busy season
exampleSpecs.audience: couples where one person is building rebuttals
exampleSpecs.stakes: loneliness may harden if it is answered with schedule facts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Javier paraphrases the sting in his own words and leaves room for correction
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "You are already preparing your defense," Sam says

exampleSpecs.domain: teacher hearing student complaint about grading
exampleSpecs.stakes: a student may be pointing at a confusing rubric, not attacking competence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam notices the competence quake and asks what part of the rubric felt unclear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of essays with colored tabs

exampleSpecs.domain: software incident postmortem with angry customer-success lead
exampleSpecs.stakes: fixing the outage depends on hearing the customer pain without judging tone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes Hiroshi two minutes to stop composing the root-cause defense and ask what customers heard first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a status page still showing yellow

exampleSpecs.domain: friend returning after months of silence
exampleSpecs.audience: friendships where timing makes paraphrase delicate
exampleSpecs.stakes: one scripted summary could sound like therapy and push the friend away
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Manon uses ordinary language to check the meaning instead of a formula
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a voicemail waveform on a cracked phone screen
mustAvoid: so what I hear you saying formula
